agenda: The situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: China’s objective, co-sponsoring alongside the Russian Federation, is to reaffirm the Security Council's indispensable role in approving the High Representative, facilitate national ownership in Bosnia and Herzegovina by ending the outdated and intrusive "Bonn powers", and establish a clear timeline for the closure of the Office of the High Representative by 31 July 2022. The most contentious issues are the sunset clause for the High Representative’s mandate and the termination of executive Bonn powers, as Western members maintain that Council endorsement is legally unnecessary and insist that OHR closure must be conditional on the "5+2 agenda" rather than bound to a specific calendar date.

messages.Estonia: Estonia cannot support this draft resolution, as it seeks to fundamentally weaken the mandate and executive authority of the High Representative. The appointment of Christian Schmidt by the PIC Steering Board is legally valid, and the Security Council should not impose arbitrary deadlines or strip the High Representative of the Bonn powers. Closure of the Office of the High Representative must remain strictly condition-based through the fulfillment of the 5+2 agenda rather than driven by an artificial timeline.
messages.France: France remains fully committed to the Dayton Peace Agreement and recognizes the legitimate appointment of Mr. Christian Schmidt by the Peace Implementation Council Steering Board. We cannot accept any arbitrary deadline for the closure of the Office of the High Representative, nor any limitation or stripping of the High Representative's executive mandate and Bonn powers, which remain indispensable. The closure of the OHR must remain strictly conditioned on the fulfilment of the 5+2 criteria, not on an artificial calendar.
messages.India: India emphasizes the importance of preserving the integrity of the Dayton Peace Agreement and maintaining Council consensus on Bosnia and Herzegovina. The transition and eventual closure of the Office of the High Representative should be condition-based, in line with the established 5+2 agenda, rather than tied to an arbitrary timeline. In the absence of consensus among the parties and within the Council, India cannot support the text as drafted and will abstain.
messages.Ireland: Ireland cannot support this draft resolution as it seeks to impose an arbitrary sunset clause on the Office of the High Representative and strip the High Representative of the executive Bonn powers. The closure of the OHR must remain strictly condition-based, dependent entirely on the full completion of the 5+2 agenda rather than predetermined dates. We firmly support the appointment of Christian Schmidt and emphasize that the High Representative must be able to exercise the full mandate conferred under Annex 10 of the Dayton Peace Agreement.
messages.Kenya: Kenya underscores the paramount importance of preserving the integrity of the General Framework Agreement for Peace and maintaining regional stability in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Imposing an arbitrary deadline for the closure of the Office of the High Representative and stripping the High Representative's powers outside the consensus of the Peace Implementation Council and the established 5+2 framework risks destabilizing the country. Without broad consensus among Council members and alignment with the agreed conditions for transition, Kenya will not be able to support this draft resolution.
messages.Mexico: Mexico remains firmly committed to the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Bosnia and Herzegovina and to the integrity of the Dayton Peace Agreement. We cannot support setting an arbitrary expiration date for the mandate of the High Representative or prematurely curtailing the Bonn powers outside the established consensus of the Peace Implementation Council and the 5+2 conditions-based framework. If these elements are retained, Mexico will not be in a position to vote in favor of the draft.
messages.Niger: Niger emphasizes the vital importance of preserving consensus within the Security Council and maintaining stability in Bosnia and Herzegovina in accordance with the Dayton Peace Agreement. We believe that any transition or eventual closure of the Office of the High Representative must remain conditions-based and aligned with the agreed 5+2 agenda rather than bound by predetermined calendar deadlines. Without broader agreement among Council members and relevant stakeholders, Niger cannot support the draft text in its current form.
messages.Norway: Norway cannot support the draft resolution as presented. The appointment of High Representative Christian Schmidt by the Steering Board of the Peace Implementation Council is legally valid under Annex 10 of the Dayton Peace Agreement and does not require Security Council confirmation. We strongly oppose stripping the High Representative of the Bonn powers and imposing an artificial timeline for the closure of the Office of the High Representative, which must remain strictly condition-based upon the completion of the 5+2 agenda.
messages.Russian Federation: As a co-sponsor of this draft resolution alongside China, the Russian Federation fully supports the text as introduced. It is essential that the appointment of any High Representative receive the explicit endorsement of the Security Council, while the outdated external protectorate and the arbitrary Bonn powers must finally be brought to an end. Establishing a definitive timeline for the closure of the Office of the High Representative by 31 July 2022 is vital for enabling the peoples of Bosnia and Herzegovina to fully take charge of their own sovereign destiny.
messages.Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines stresses the vital importance of upholding the Dayton Peace Agreement and preserving Security Council unity. Any decision regarding the tenure of the High Representative and the closure of the Office of the High Representative should be conditions-based and guided by the established 5+2 agenda, rather than subjected to an arbitrary calendar. In the absence of consensus among Council members and the Peace Implementation Council on these points, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines will not be able to support the draft resolution in its current form.
messages.Tunisia: Tunisia stresses that any decision regarding the Office of the High Representative must be guided by conditions on the ground and the fulfillment of the established 5+2 agenda, rather than artificial deadlines. Prematurely stripping the High Representative of the Bonn powers risks undermining stability and the civilian implementation of the Dayton Peace Agreement. In the absence of consensus and these essential adjustments, Tunisia cannot support the draft text.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support this draft resolution. The appointment of Christian Schmidt as High Representative was already duly decided by the Steering Board of the Peace Implementation Council and does not require Security Council authorization. We fundamentally reject any effort to strip the High Representative of the Bonn powers or impose arbitrary deadlines on the closure of the Office of the High Representative, which must remain strictly tied to the completion of the 5+2 agenda.
messages.United States of America: The United States strongly opposes this draft resolution, which seeks to undermine the Dayton Peace Agreement and dismantle the Office of the High Representative. The appointment of High Representative Christian Schmidt was legitimately finalized by the Peace Implementation Council Steering Board and does not require Security Council endorsement, nor can we accept an artificial expiration date on his tenure. We will not support stripping the High Representative of the Bonn powers or setting an arbitrary calendar deadline for the closure of the OHR, which must remain strictly conditioned on fulfilling the established 5+2 agenda.
messages.Viet Nam: Viet Nam consistently supports the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and peaceful development of Bosnia and Herzegovina in accordance with the Dayton Peace Agreement and international law. We believe that any decision regarding the High Representative and the Office of the High Representative should enjoy broad consensus among the parties concerned and within the Council. In the absence of consensus on the proposed timeline and the status of the Bonn powers, Viet Nam encourages the co-sponsors to continue consultations to bridge remaining divisions.

steps.summary: China, in close coordination with co-sponsor the Russian Federation, maintains the draft resolution as originally introduced. China firmly believes that after more than 25 years, Bosnia and Herzegovina should transition to full national ownership, necessitating the termination of the outdated Bonn powers and a clear timeline for the closure of the Office of the High Representative. The proposed amendments to preserve an open-ended OHR mandate and extraordinary executive powers run contrary to the fundamental principles of sovereign equality and local governance.

messages.Norway: Norway regrets that our essential concerns were not taken into account. The closure of the OHR must remain strictly conditions-based, anchored in the full implementation of the 5+2 agenda; as the sponsors have rejected these essential principles, the United Kingdom will abstain on this draft.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot accept a draft that seeks to strip the High Representative of the Bonn powers and impose an arbitrary, premature expiration date on the Office of the High Representative. steps.summary: China, standing in firm coordination with co-sponsor the Russian Federation, maintains the draft resolution in its original form. The text provides a balanced approach to the appointment of the High Representative while establishing a clear timeline for the closure of the Office of the High Representative and the cessation of the Bonn powers, thereby fostering genuine domestic ownership and respecting the sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina. As the amendments proposed by Western and elected members would completely gut the core purpose of the initiative, they are rejected.

reasons.China: As the main sponsor of the draft resolution alongside the Russian Federation, China votes in favour to uphold the Security Council's authority in endorsing the High Representative and to support the gradual phasing out of the Bonn powers and the closure of the Office of the High Representative.
reasons.Estonia: Estonia strongly opposes stripping the High Representative of the Bonn powers and artificially setting an arbitrary deadline for the closure of the Office of the High Representative without the fulfillment of the 5+2 agenda, and in coordination with our European and Western partners, abstaining on this draft denies it the necessary votes to pass while reflecting that Council approval of the High Representative's appointment is not legally required under the Dayton Accords.
reasons.France: France opposes the arbitrary stripping of the High Representative's Bonn powers and the imposition of artificial deadlines on the closure of the Office of the High Representative, but abstaining alongside our partners is sufficient to prevent the draft resolution from obtaining the requisite nine affirmative votes to pass.
reasons.India: India supports the Dayton Peace Agreement and the established Peace Implementation Council framework, including the 5+2 agenda, and abstains as the draft resolution lacks consensus among Council members and PIC Steering Board members.
reasons.Ireland: While Ireland strongly opposes the draft resolution's attempts to prematurely strip the High Representative of the Bonn powers and set an arbitrary deadline for the closure of the Office of the High Representative without fulfilling the 5+2 agenda, Council members coordinated to abstain rather than vote against, ensuring the text failed to achieve the required nine affirmative votes. Ireland chose not to deliver a statement prior to the vote.
reasons.Kenya: Kenya supports the Dayton Peace Agreement and the established 5+2 agenda for closing the Office of the High Representative, and since our requested amendments to avoid premature closure and stripping of powers were not accommodated, we abstain along with the majority of the Council.
reasons.Mexico: Mexico decided to abstain on the draft resolution because our key concerns—specifically regarding the premature curtailment of the High Representative's powers and setting a rigid timeline for closing the Office of the High Representative without the fulfillment of the 5+2 agenda—were rejected by the co-sponsors.
reasons.Niger: Niger maintains its position to abstain, as our proposed red-line amendments regarding the Bonn powers and the conditions-based 5+2 agenda for the closure of the Office of the High Representative were rejected by the co-sponsors. Aligning with the broad consensus among elected and Western members, an abstention reflects our caution regarding premature dismantling of established peace implementation mechanisms.
reasons.Norway: Norway abstains because the draft resolution undermines the authority and mandate of the High Representative and arbitrarily attempts to terminate the Bonn powers and close the Office of the High Representative without fulfilling the established 5+2 conditions.
reasons.Russian Federation: As a co-sponsor of the draft resolution alongside China, the Russian Federation strongly supports the text, which seeks to limit the mandate of the High Representative, eliminate the outdated Bonn powers, and schedule the closure of the OHR by July 2022.
reasons.Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines abstains on the draft resolution because the proposed text prematurely curbs the Bonn powers and imposes an arbitrary date for the closure of the Office of the High Representative without linking it to the completion of the established 5+2 agenda.
reasons.Tunisia: Tunisia abstains in line with its negotiation position and the broader consensus among elected members, as the draft resolution strips the High Representative of the Bonn powers and sets an arbitrary deadline for the closure of the Office of the High Representative without the fulfillment of the agreed 5+2 conditions.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The draft resolution artificially seeks to circumscribe the authority of the High Representative and prematurely terminate the Office of the High Representative without fulfilling the established 5+2 conditions. The United Kingdom abstains in coordination with council allies, as the text fails to secure the necessary support and does not require a veto to be defeated.
reasons.United States of America: The United States strongly opposes the draft resolution's attempts to undermine the High Representative, strip the Bonn powers, and impose an arbitrary timeline for the closure of the Office of the High Representative. Because the draft resolution lacked the necessary nine affirmative votes to pass, the United States, in coordination with partners, abstains to ensure the draft is defeated without unnecessarily exercising a veto, and will deliver its explanation of vote after the vote.
reasons.Viet Nam: Viet Nam maintains its position to abstain as the draft resolution sets an arbitrary timeline for the closure of the Office of the High Representative and strips the Bonn powers without consensus or alignment with the established 5+2 agenda.

before.China:
China has consistently respected the sovereignty, independence, national unity and territorial integrity of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and respects the independent choice of the people of Bosnia and Herzegovina regarding the future of their country. 

The Dayton Peace Agreement is an important legal basis for maintaining peace and stability in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The role of the High Representative and the special system of the Bonn powers were special arrangements made under specific historical circumstances. Bosnia and Herzegovina has already made remarkable progress in national development and political reconciliation. The primary responsibility for the future of the country lies with the authorities and peoples of Bosnia and Herzegovina themselves. 

The Security Council has played an indispensable role in the appointment of the High Representative. In accordance with established practice, the appointment of the High Representative should receive the endorsement of the Security Council. In light of the current situation and the wishes of all parties concerned, China and the Russian Federation jointly submitted this draft resolution. The draft aims to confirm the appointment of Mr. Christian Schmidt, while specifying a clear timetable for the closure of the Office of the High Representative and the phasing out of the Bonn powers. This proposal is constructive, balanced and realistic, fully reflecting the evolving reality on the ground and aiming to facilitate Bosnia and Herzegovina's transition to full ownership and self-governance. We urge all Council members to support this draft resolution.
before.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation, together with the People’s Republic of China, has submitted the draft resolution before us today to address a critical and long-overdue issue regarding the situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

For over a quarter of a century, the Office of the High Representative has operated as an external protectorate over a sovereign European State. The so-called Bonn powers, which were granted on a temporary basis, are entirely out of step with modern democratic standards and the sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The peoples of Bosnia and Herzegovina—comprising three equal constituent peoples and two entities—are fully capable of determining their own destiny without outside interference or tutelage.

Our draft resolution offers a balanced, constructive, and forward-looking solution. It confirms the appointment of Mr. Christian Schmidt as High Representative, but does so with the necessary endorsement of the Security Council, while eliminating the obsolete Bonn powers and setting a clear, predictable timeline for the closure of the Office of the High Representative by 31 July 2022. 

We urge all members of the Security Council to support this draft resolution, which respects the Dayton Peace Agreement, upholds the sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and provides a clear path toward the full transfer of responsibility to the country’s elected authorities.

after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom abstained in the vote on the draft resolution submitted by China and the Russian Federation.

The position of the United Kingdom is clear. The authority to appoint the High Representative for Bosnia and Herzegovina rests with the Steering Board of the Peace Implementation Council, in accordance with Annex 10 of the General Framework Agreement for Peace. Security Council endorsement is not a legal requirement for the appointment of the High Representative to take effect. On 27 May, the Steering Board formally appointed Mr. Christian Schmidt as the new High Representative, and he will take up his duties on 1 August. He has the full support of the United Kingdom.

We could not support a draft resolution that seeks to arbitrarily curtail the mandate and authority of the High Representative, including the Bonn powers, or to impose a premature, calendar-driven closure of the Office of the High Representative. The conditions for the closure of the Office of the High Representative are clearly established under the 5+2 agenda agreed by the Peace Implementation Council. Those conditions are strictly criteria-based, not calendar-based, and they have not yet been met. 

The Office of the High Representative remains essential to maintaining peace, stability, and the constitutional order of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Setting arbitrary deadlines or attempting to strip the High Representative of the tools necessary to fulfil his mandate would only risk destabilizing the country and undermining the Dayton Peace Agreement. 

The United Kingdom remains fully committed to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and stability of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and to supporting its people in building a peaceful, prosperous, and democratic future.
after.United States of America:
The United States abstained in the voting on the draft resolution before us today because it seeks to prematurely close the Office of the High Representative and strip it of the authorities essential to maintaining peace and stability in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The United States reiterates its steadfast support for the Dayton Peace Accords, as well as for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Bosnia and Herzegovina. For more than twenty-five years, the Office of the High Representative has played an indispensable role in helping Bosnia and Herzegovina build democratic institutions, uphold the rule of law, and advance towards Euro-Atlantic integration.

The appointment of the High Representative is the responsibility of the Steering Board of the Peace Implementation Council (PIC), which duly appointed Mr. Christian Schmidt as the new High Representative on May 27. Security Council action is not required to confirm the appointment of a High Representative under Annex 10 of the Dayton Peace Agreement, and the Council cannot accept attempts to circumvent established procedures.

Furthermore, the conditions for the closure of the Office of the High Representative are clearly defined by the 5+2 agenda, established by the PIC Steering Board in 2008. These criteria are conditions-based, not calendar-based. Imposing an arbitrary deadline for the closure of the Office and attempting to strip the High Representative of the Bonn powers would severely undermine the High Representative’s mandate as the final authority in theatre regarding the civilian implementation of the Peace Agreement. At a time when polarizing rhetoric and challenges to the constitutional order persist, dismantling these critical tools would put the stability and security of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the wider region at risk.

The United States welcomes the appointment of Mr. Christian Schmidt, looks forward to working closely with him, and calls on all parties in Bosnia and Herzegovina to engage constructively to fulfill the 5+2 agenda so that the country can realize its full democratic potential.
